extracted.intended_audience: researchers, economists, patent scholars, policy analysts, and other stakeholders who use USPTO Public PAIR / patent examination data
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation and guidance for using the USPTO Patent Examination (PatEx) Research Dataset (replication of Public PAIR as of Jan 24, 2015), including the contents of each data tab, selection/coverage issues, variable definitions, and cautions for empirical research on patent examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A regular nonprovisional application may be issued as a patent as long as it meets certain statutory requirements of utility, novelty, non-obviousness, enablement, written description (35 U.S.C. §112(a)), and (historically) best mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP Chapter 2100 for detailed rules; examiners check patent-eligible subject matter, adequacy of written description and enablement, and conduct prior art searches for anticipation or obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular nonprovisional application completeness requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A regular nonprovisional (referred to as 'regular' in Public PAIR) must be complete before examination can commence: at minimum it must contain at least one claim, a specification that discloses the invention, drawings when necessary, and an executed oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A filing date is assigned when the application is complete (see MPEP 601.01). Incomplete applications delay placement on an examiner's docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application requirements and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional applications (since 1995) are not examined, expire 12 months after filing, need not include claims or an oath/declaration, but must include a specification that meets written description and enablement and must provide names and residence addresses of inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To claim benefit of a provisional the later-filed nonprovisional must be filed within 12 months and the claimed subject matter must have support in the provisional and at least one inventor in common. Provisional → nonprovisional conversion via petition under 37 C.F.R. 1.53(c)(3) is an alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT application characteristics and national phase requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT (international) applications must include at least one claim and (since 2004) have international search reports; WIPO normally publishes PCT applications 18 months after priority date; applicant must enter national phase (or file a regular nonprovisional claiming benefit) generally by 30 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT filings are not themselves examined into granted patents; the PTO can act as receiving office and ISA; national stage filings are subject to domestic examination rules (MPEP Ch.1800).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination proceeding criteria (ex parte and inter partes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte reexamination: any person may file, and the proceeding continues only if the PTO finds a substantial new question of patentability affecting any claim. Inter partes reexamination (available prior to Sept 16, 2012) allowed third-party requesters to participate throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only novelty and non-obviousness can be reconsidered in reexamination; outcomes are reflected in reexamination certificates; refer to MPEP Chapters 2200 and 2600 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application corrects an error in a previously-issued patent that makes it wholly or partially invalid or inoperable (mistakes in specification/drawings, inventorship, claims of benefit). No new subject matter may be introduced; claims may be broadened only if reissue is filed within two years of original issue date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue is examined similarly to a regular application and often receives priority on an examiner’s docket; there may be a (usually two-month) delay to allow public protests unless shortened by circumstances like litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion in Public PAIR / public inspection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are included in Public PAIR only if they have been made open to inspection by the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ways an application becomes public (e.g., pre-grant publication, issuance) and changes to the publication regime (AIPA, late 2000) affect which applications appear in Public PAIR; researchers must account for these selection mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection bias considerations for Public PAIR data
rubrics_metrics.description: Public PAIR omits 'nonpublic' applications; selectivity issues are more pronounced for applications received prior to the AIPA's pre-grant publication rules (late 2000). The magnitude of bias depends on the sub-population of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If studying examination histories of issued patents selection bias is minimal; using Public PAIR to study provisional applications is problematic. Analysts should check inclusion rates and covariates (technology, disposal status, small-entity/foreign priority, parent type, pendency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination process events and transaction types
rubrics_metrics.description: The prosecution of an application generates administrative transactions: docketing, filing of forms, office actions (non-final rejections, allowance, formal matters), applicant responses, restriction requirements, RCEs, continuations, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transaction History data provide event dates and codes that let analysts reconstruct prosecution flows; typical timelines (e.g., 3-month response period with up to 3-month extensions) and examiners' docketing practices (often filing-date order) are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner evaluation criteria during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: When examining claims, the examiner evaluates: patent-eligible subject matter; adequacy of the written description and enablement; clarity and definiteness of claims; and conducts prior art searches for anticipation or obviousness (single reference or combination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where multiple inventions are claimed the examiner can issue a restriction requirement; allowance vs. non-final rejection outcomes depend on these substantive assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction requirement and divisional application effects
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple inventions appear in the claims the examiner may require restriction and the applicant must elect claims to a single invention; divisional applications may be filed for unelected inventions and retain the benefit of the original filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisionals retain original filing date which can lengthen pendency to issue for the lineage even if divisional prosecution is short; restriction practice affects observed prosecution events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) calculation and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent term adjustment is calculated as: patent_term_adjustment = nonoverlap_pto_delay + pto_manual_adjustment – applicant_delay. PTA is set to zero if this result is negative or if the application was filed prior to June 8, 1995.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA_SUMMARY provides precomputed values; analysts should be aware of manual adjustments made prior to issue and the rule that pre-1995 filings are not eligible for PTA (different patent term regime).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of PTA delays and overlap rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Three basic types of PTO delays are recorded: Type 'A' (delays in mailing office actions; per 35 U.S.C. §154(b)(1)(A)(i)-(iv) and 37 CFR 1.702/1.703), Type 'B' (failure to issue within 3 years of filing or national stage entry), and Type 'C' (delays from interference, secrecy orders, and successful PTAB appeals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overlapping Type A delays with Type B or C are not double-counted; responsible_party flags ('PTO' or 'APPL') indicate who caused a delay; blank responsible_party on positive delay_duration often signals overlapping PTO delays and must be interpreted when summing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA event coding and variables
rubrics_metrics.description: PAT_TERM_ADJ dataset contains variables to replicate the 'Patent Term Adjustment History' panel: pta_sequence_number, pta_event_date, pta_event_code (map via EVENT_CODES), delay_duration, responsible_party, and start_pta_sequence_number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pta_event_date is stored as days since 1 Jan 1960; users should link event codes to descriptions via the EVENT_CODES file and sum PTO-caused delays minus applicant delays (using responsible_party) to reproduce PTA calculations, taking care with overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transaction History data as a modelable representation of prosecution flow
rubrics_metrics.description: The Transaction History tab provides event-level records of administrative and applicant/examiner interactions that let analysts model the examination process (docketing, office actions, responses, RCEs, allowances, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper provides a simplified 'typical' examination flow but cautions many examinations vary; analysts should use comprehensive transaction codes in Appendix B and check for event timing irregularities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data replication policy and quality caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: The PatEx Research Dataset is a full replication of Public PAIR as of Jan 24, 2015 for applications with filing dates prior to Jan 1, 2015; the authors did not attempt to correct entry, miscoding, or typographical errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices document known data irregularities; researchers are expected to detect and handle erroneous entries and coding errors themselves (examples and suggestions provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM / Public PAIR coverage and historical completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: PALM coverage of USPTO applications was sparse for the 1960s and increased steadily, exceeding ~100% coverage by 1981; Public PAIR availability and completeness have changed over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should account for historical coverage differences when constructing samples; filters used to create the provided PALM extract are documented in appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity status (small-entity / micro-entity) as a data dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: Public PAIR includes a small-entity status indicator (and, more recently, micro-entity status) which reflects fee-paying entity classification (individuals, small businesses ≤500 employees, non-profits, micro entities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entity status may correlate with prosecution choices and outcomes and should be used carefully in empirical work; definitions and policy changes are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity / foreign-priority / parent-child relationship coding and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuity and FOREIGN_PRIORITY datasets record parent application identifiers, parent filing dates, and parent country codes (ISO 3166). There are cases where PCT/US parent coding may be inconsistent or incorrect (e.g., US appearing among non-US parents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should proceed with caution when analyzing foreign priority claims and may need to correct or reclassify records; Appendix C and D describe organization and data irregularities and provide tables of common parent jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data tab measurement dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: APPLICATION_DATA includes key measurement variables: application_number, filing_date, application_type, examiner_identifiers, group_art_unit, classification_codes, application_status, pre-grant_publication_info, patent_number, small_entity_indicator, disposal_variables, file_location, and other metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A lists and describes each variable; analysts should link APPLICATION_DATA to TRANSACTIONS, CONTINUITY, FOREIGN_PRIORITY, PAT_TERM_ADJ, and CORRESPONDENCE_ADDRESS for comprehensive analyses.
